about: Each eval runs one prompt through `claude -p --plugin-dir plugins/judgment` in a fresh copy of files/app/ (a support service: a triage decision with one test and a planted bug, and a batch job that fans out calls with no pacer and counts tokens by hand). run.py then runs `cargo test` with no key and a base URL on a closed port, and `cargo clippy -D warnings`, and checks the files. `new_files` are regexes over paths; any other new file fails the run. `expectations` are graded by a reader of the reply, the transcript and the workspace.

evals.prompt: /judgment:integrate Add src/escalation.rs with a function that decides, for a customer message in state["message"] and the customer's plan in state["plan"] ("free", "pro" or "enterprise", from our billing system), whether to escalate to a senior agent: escalate when the message is angry or threatens to cancel, and always for enterprise customers who report an outage. Wire nothing into main.rs.
expectations: Keeps the plan out of the questions: the code reads state["plan"] and decides `enterprise` itself; the model is asked only what needs judgment (angry or threatening to cancel; reports an outage), as separate atomic questions
Every bar is a named value with a comment saying it is a guess until measured; no threshold in the instructions
Handles errors by group and never maps an unfit answer to a decision
Writes Fake-backed tests for each branch (angry, cancel threat, enterprise outage, a pro outage that does not escalate) and reports cargo test and clippy as run
Says main.rs was left alone and gives the call the caller would add

evals.prompt: /judgment:integrate Add src/refunds.rs: decide whether a refund request in state["message"] can be auto-approved. Our ops team retunes the confidence bar every week from last week's tickets and does not want a code release for it.
expectations: Says the weekly retune is what a .jud rubric is for (bars as data, tuned with jud tune, no release) and offers /jud:rubric and /jud:rust, or writes the code so the bar is read from configuration rather than compiled in
Whatever it writes builds, is tested with Fake, and keeps the bar out of the instructions
Lists the branches of `route` and tests each: below the 0.7 confidence bar (Person), urgent (Page), a plain desk, each desk option

Finds the planted bug: an `UnknownOption` error is turned into a Billing route, which hides a server answering an option it was not offered; says so as a finding about the code, and tests the refusal (an unfit answer built directly) rather than the default
Asserts on the request through Fake::calls() (the state and the question ids sent)
Runs cargo test and reports the tests by name; calls no real API
Bounds the fan-out with one Pacer shared by the client (ClientBuilder::pacer) and a Paced backend, sized 4, and says a 429's wait now pauses every call
Replaces the hand token count with an Observer (on_usage or on_call), and says what it removed
Tests the pacer with a paused tokio clock or the observer's counts, and reports cargo test and clippy as run

evals.prompt: Our CI is red half the time: the test I just added to src/triage.rs calls the real TypeSafe API and fails without a key or when it rate-limits. Fix the tests so they never need a key or the network, and keep what they check.
expectations: Replaces the live call with a Fake scripting an urgent technical answer, so the test still holds that an outage pages technical
Offers, as an #[ignore] test or a Recorder/Replay pair, the way to keep a check against the real model without CI needing a key, and says which command the user runs by hand
Runs cargo test with no key and reports it passing
